description: Wire vectors of the JoinGroup API (key 11, v0 to v9), replayed by tests/Compliance.

vectors.description: JoinGroup request v1 of a client that has no member id yet: the rebalance_timeout of Kafka 0.10.1 (30000) sits between the session timeout (10000) and the member id, and it does not have to lie inside the group.min/max.session.timeout.ms of the broker.

The answer to the version 1 request: the frame of version 0, unchanged - JOIN_GROUP_RESPONSE_V1 is JOIN_GROUP_RESPONSE_V0 in Protocol.java @ 0.10.2.2 - for the first and only member of a fresh group, which is its leader and therefore receives the metadata of every member.

JoinGroup request v0 of a client that has no member id yet, offering the `range` protocol of the `consumer` protocol type with its subscription as opaque metadata. There is no rebalance timeout between the session timeout and the member id: a 0.10.2.2 broker then uses the session timeout as the rebalance timeout as well.

JoinGroup answer of the first and only member of a group: the assigned member id, the generation 1, the selected protocol and the member itself as the leader, whose answer carries the metadata of every member.
JoinGroup request v0 with a session timeout below group.min.session.timeout.ms of the broker.
JoinGroup answer for a session timeout the broker does not allow: the error code 26, generation -1 and empty ids.
JoinGroup request v2 of the first member of a group, the frame of v1 with a higher version field.
The answer v2: the throttle time, and then the generation of a v1 answer with the member as its own leader.

JoinGroup request v3 of the first member of a group, the frame of v2 with a higher version field. The member metadata is a real `Subscription` of the `consumer` protocol: a 2.x coordinator parses it, see "Broker quirks and observations".
The answer v3 to that join: the throttle time, the generation 1, the protocol the coordinator picked and the member that is the leader of the generation, with its metadata in the members array.

JoinGroup request v4 of a client that has no member id yet - the `member_id` is the empty string. This is the request KIP-394 refuses: from version 4 on the coordinator does not add a member it cannot identify to a rebalance.

The refusal: the error code **79** (`MemberIdRequired`) with the generation -1, an empty group protocol, an empty leader id and no members - and the member id the coordinator generated for this client in `member_id`, which the next join has to send. It arrives immediately: no rebalance was started and no member was added.
The very same request again, with the member id the 79 answer carried. It is byte for byte the frame above except for that field.
The answer to the second join: the generation 1, the protocol the coordinator picked, and the member as the leader of its own group with its metadata in the members array.

JoinGroup request v5 of a **static** member (KIP-345): the `group_instance_id` `t3-345-one` stands behind an empty `member_id`. A join that names an instance id is never refused with the 79 of KIP-394 - `requireKnownMemberId` is `version >= 4 && groupInstanceId.isEmpty` in `KafkaApis.handleJoinGroupRequest` @ 2.8.2 - so this one request joins the group.

The answer: the generation 1 and the member id the coordinator generated, which for a static member is `<group.instance.id>-<uuid>` and not `<client.id>-<uuid>`. Every entry of the member array carries the `group_instance_id` that version 5 added, here the very instance that joined.

JoinGroup request v6 (KIP-482) of a static member: the same fields as version 5 with compact strings, a compact protocol array and a tag buffer after every structure - the header, every entry of `group_protocols` and the body.
The answer v6: the member array is compact, every member entry ends in its own tag buffer and so does the body.

JoinGroup request v7 (Kafka 2.5, KIP-559): byte for byte the flexible version 6 frame with the version field 7 - "Version 7 is the same as version 6" in `JoinGroupRequest.json` @ 2.8.2 - sent with the member id the coordinator had just assigned. What the version states is that the client understands the two protocol fields of the answer.

The answer v7 of an accepted join: the nullable `protocol_type` of KIP-559 stands in front of the protocol name, both as compact strings - `consumer` and the `range` the coordinator selected - so a member can check that the group it joined is of the kind it asked for.

The first join of a dynamic member, with an **empty** member id: the 79 of KIP-394 is answered to a version 7 exactly as it is to a version 4, and the frame is the one above with a zero-length compact member id.

The refusal: the error code **79** with the member id the coordinator generated - and, from version 7 on, a **null** `protocol_type` and a **null** `protocol_name`, both the single byte `00` of a null compact string, where a version 6 answer carries the empty string of `GroupCoordinator.NoProtocol` in the name and has no type at all.

JoinGroup request v8 (Kafka 3.2, KIP-800): the first join of a dynamic member, which carries no member id yet, with the `reason` the version added behind the protocol array - a compact string, the last field of the body in front of its tag buffer.

The 79 MemberIdRequired of KIP-394 at version 8: the answer is the one of version 7, field for field - "Version 8 is the same as version 7" - with the generation -1, a null protocol type and name, an empty leader and the member id the coordinator assigned. The reason of the refused join is NOT logged by the node: only the join that follows it names one in the broker log.

The join that follows, with the assigned member id and the reason the Java consumer sends for it. The node logs it: "Preparing to rebalance group … client reason: need to re-join with the given member-id: …".

fields.reason: need to re-join with the given member-id: kafka-client-t3-32-6cf42ab9-8bfd-4603-a1ff-3590c274829c

vectors.description: The accepted answer v8, held for the 3 s of `group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms`: the generation 1, the protocol type and name of KIP-559 and the one member of the group, because this member is its leader. There is no `skip_assignment` byte anywhere in it - that is what version 9 adds.

JoinGroup request v9 (Kafka 3.2, KIP-814), the version this client sends: the frame of version 8, field for field - "Version 9 is the same as version 8" - with the api version 9 in the header, because what the version buys sits in the answer.

The 79 of KIP-394 at version 9: the one byte of `skip_assignment` stands between the empty leader id and the member id the coordinator assigned, and it is **false**, as it is in every error answer of the api.
The join that follows at version 9, with the assigned member id and the reason of the Java consumer.

vectors.description: The accepted answer v9 of the leader of a fresh generation: `skip_assignment` is **false**, so this leader computes the assignment out of the member array that follows it and publishes it with a SyncGroup.

The first join of a STATIC member at version 9, which names its `group.instance.id` and **no reason at all**: the null reason is the single byte 00 of a compact null, the last field of the body in front of its tag buffer. A join that carries an instance id is never refused with the 79 of KIP-394.

Its answer, held for the 3 s of `group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms`: the generation 1, the member id the coordinator built out of the instance id and a uuid, and `skip_assignment` **false** - the group had no assignment yet, so its leader has to compute one.

The frame KIP-814 exists for: the same static instance comes back after a restart with an EMPTY member id - it lost the one of the previous generation - and the `group.instance.id` that the group still holds.

The answer that carries `skip_assignment` = **true** (the byte 01 behind the leader id): the coordinator did not rebalance the group at all - it answered in milliseconds, the generation is still 1 - it only replaced the member id of that instance, and this member is the leader. The leader must therefore NOT compute an assignment: it sends a SyncGroup with an empty assignment array and is answered the assignment the generation already agreed on.
